title: Stable talk (expert)
description: An experienced presenter covers every essential point at a steady pace. The system should stay quiet.

events.transcript_chunk: Every week researchers skim dozens of papers, and dense passages pull us into re-reading loops.
A static PDF cannot react when a reader struggles, and today's highlighting tools are manual.
GazeFlow uses an ordinary webcam to track gaze and detect regressions, the moments you jump back to re-read.
When a regression lands on a dense term, a glossary pop-up appears. It all runs locally, and no video is stored.

ground_truth.note: A 2.2 s pause for emphasis is natural.

events.transcript_chunk: We ran a within-subjects study with 24 participants. The baseline was the same reader without adaptation.
Comprehension went up 18% over the baseline, reading time was unchanged, and NASA-TLX workload dropped.
So the adaptation helps without slowing anyone down.
The main limitation: in low light, webcam accuracy drops, and we only tested short lab sessions.
The takeaway: attention-aware documents are feasible today with commodity webcams. Next, a field deployment.
Thank you, I'm happy to take questions.
